first: In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people’s sense of responsibility.
body: In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people’s sense of responsibility. As the future builders of the country, young people will soon take on key roles in every field, and how responsibly they act will largely shape the future of society.

A strong sense of responsibility matters on two levels. For individuals, it is the foundation of success: students who take their studies seriously and keep their promises are far more likely to earn the trust of teachers, employers and friends. For society, responsible young people are a major driving force behind progress. In recent years, countless young volunteers have taught in rural schools, cared for elderly residents and joined environmental campaigns, showing that a sense of duty can turn into concrete action.

Enhancing this sense of responsibility requires joint efforts. Families should let children handle their own affairs and face the consequences of their choices, while schools can offer more opportunities for community service. Most importantly, young people themselves should start with small things, such as finishing every task carefully and caring for those around them. Only in this way can they shoulder the responsibilities of their time.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
first: With the trend of urbanization, it is vitally important for city residents to develop a stronger love for nature.
body: With the trend of urbanization, it is vitally important for city residents to develop a stronger love for nature. Surrounded by concrete buildings, many people now spend most of their time indoors and seldom notice the changing seasons, let alone the birds and trees around them.

A deeper love for nature benefits both individuals and the city as a whole. For one thing, time spent in green spaces relieves stress and refreshes the mind. After a busy week, a walk in a park or along a river can do more for our mood than hours of scrolling through our phones. For another, people who cherish nature are more willing to protect it in their daily lives. They tend to sort their waste, save water and use public transportation, making the city cleaner and more livable.

To cultivate such love, city governments should build more parks and green spaces in every neighborhood, and schools can organize outdoor activities so that children learn to observe plants and animals. Residents, too, can start simply by stepping outside and appreciating the natural world around them. After all, a city that respects nature is a better home for everyone.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
first: Faced with growing globalization, students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence.
body: Faced with growing globalization, students realize that a deep understanding of traditional Chinese culture helps cultivate cultural confidence. Amid the flood of foreign films, brands and ideas, young people who know little about their own heritage may easily lose their bearings. Some even look down on their own traditions as outdated.

Such understanding builds confidence in two ways. To begin with, it gives students a firm sense of identity. Once they appreciate the wisdom of classics such as The Analects or the beauty of Tang poetry, they see their culture not as old-fashioned but as a source of pride. Moreover, it allows them to introduce China to the world with confidence. A friend of mine who studied in Britain told me that her classmates were fascinated when she explained the meaning behind Spring Festival couplets, an experience that made her proud of where she came from.

Therefore, students should make a conscious effort to explore traditional culture, whether by reading classical works, visiting museums or learning a traditional art such as calligraphy. Firmly rooted in their own culture, young people can stay open-minded without losing themselves in a globalized world.
